Competitive intelligence is the practice of gathering and analyzing information about competitors, such as their product launches, pricing, messaging, and market positioning, to inform your own strategy. In a brand context, it helps you understand how your brand is perceived relative to others and spot opportunities or risks in the market.

Brand monitoring catches scams, fake accounts, and counterfeit products before they reach large numbers of customers. Every phishing site or fake profile removed is one less negative experience tied to your name. Brand Intelligence focuses on protecting your brand: detecting impersonation, fraud, and misuse of your name, logos, and trademarks across digital channels. Market Intelligence focuses on understanding the market: customer needs, industry trends, competitor activity, and growth opportunities. What happens if my email is on the dark web?

Your email has likely been exposed in a data breach, often together with passwords, names, or other personal details. Criminals can use it for phishing, credential stuffing (trying the leaked password on other sites), spam, or identity fraud. Change any reused passwords, turn on multi-factor authentication, and watch for suspicious messages.

Yes. Many consumer services, including some password managers, identity theft protection plans, and free tools like Have I Been Pwned, alert individuals when their email, passwords, or personal details appear in breaches.

A dark web scan is a one-time check of known breach databases for your email, domain, or credentials. It’s a useful snapshot, but it only shows past exposures. New leaks happen constantly, so continuous monitoring is needed to catch threats as they appear and respond before the data is exploited.
